candidates.material: C (graphene, sp2 carbon; monolayer favoured, few-layer or turbostratic not excluded)
candidates.evidence: Three bands at 1344.5 (D), 1580.3 (G) and 2681.2 cm-1 (2D). G matches the literature graphene origin 1581.6 cm-1 (Lee 2012) within 1.3 cm-1, and 2D matches 2676.9 cm-1 (Lee 2012, 514.5 nm) within 4 cm-1, though the laser wavelength is unknown so the 2D comparison is weak. The library matcher ranks graphene first (score 0.79, matches G and 2D). D is the defect-activated band and is absent from the matcher table, so it is unexplained there. A single sharp 2D and a G width near 25 cm-1 rule out graphite and amorphous carbon.

Rejected. The matcher score of 0.59 comes from explaining only the 2681 cm-1 band with a fitted scale of 1.038; the 1344 and 1580 cm-1 bands are unmatched. A hydrated strontium oxide is not a plausible product of CVD growth on Au and cannot give a G/D/2D pattern.
Rejected for the same reason: a single-band match at 2681 cm-1 (B1), with 1344 and 1580 cm-1 unexplained. Not a carbon material.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint null), so this is an identify task. The fitted D, G and 2D bands form the graphene pattern. The library's top candidate is graphene (literature table, lit:graphene, score 0.79, matching G and 2D). The top CRD hits are inorganic hydrates that each explain only the 2681 cm-1 band and are rejected. Laser wavelength is not stated, so the 2D position cannot be checked against the 514.5 nm reference, and the strain/doping and defect-distance relations do not apply.

peaks.irrep: A1' (D3h, monolayer); A1g in D6h bulk labels
peaks.source: Position measured by fit (1344.5 +/- 1.0 cm-1, FWHM 34.0 +/- 3.2). Assignment inferred: D band near 1350 cm-1 at visible excitation, defect-activated, about half the 2D frequency (Ferrari et al. PRL 97, 187401, 2006, via reference/materials.md). Its position is not in the curated table, so the matcher did not use it.

peaks.assignment: G (in-plane E2g stretch of sp2 carbon)
peaks.irrep: E2' (D3h, monolayer); E2g in D6h bulk labels
peaks.source: Lee, Ahn, Shim, Lee, Ryu, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012), arXiv 1209.0234, origin omega_G^0 = 1581.6 cm-1 (graphene at 514.5 nm, unstrained, undoped). Fitted 1580.3 +/- 0.9 cm-1, 1.3 cm-1 below origin, which is within calibration uncertainty; no Si reference in the file.

peaks.assignment: 2D (second-order overtone of the iTO phonon near K)
peaks.irrep: A1' (D3h, monolayer); A1g in D6h bulk labels
peaks.source: Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012), arXiv 1209.0234, origin omega_2D^0 = 2676.9 cm-1 at 514.5 nm; Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006), arXiv cond-mat/0606284 (2D about 2700 at 514 nm). Fitted 2681.2 +/- 0.4 cm-1 (full fit); FWHM 39.7 +/- 1.8 in a local 2550-2800 cm-1 refit. The 2D band disperses with laser energy, so this comparison holds only if the laser is near 514.5 nm.

properties.name: material
properties.source: Assignment of the G, D and 2D bands (Ferrari et al. 2006; Lee et al. 2012) and rejection of the CRD candidates (Bagheri and Komsa 2023) given the Au substrate and CVD origin

properties.name: phase
properties.source: Single Lorentzian 2D, rule from graphene_layers_from_2D_shape (Ferrari et al. 2006)

properties.name: layers
properties.value: 1 (monolayer favoured, moderate confidence; few-layer not excluded)
properties.source: rl.py apply_relation graphene_layers_from_2D_shape with n_2D_components=1 (Ferrari et al. PRL 97, 187401, 2006). The tool reported high confidence, but I downgrade it to moderate: 2D FWHM 35 to 40 cm-1 sits between monolayer (about 25 to 30) and turbostratic (about 50), and I_2D/I_G = 2.85 (height) is below the monolayer value of about 4 quoted by Ferrari 2006 on SiO2, which is also affected by substrate.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: I_D/I_G = 109.4/115.0 = 0.95 (peak heights) with G FWHM 24.8 cm-1, well above the 14 cm-1 low-defect value (Cancado et al. Nano Lett. 11, 3190, 2011, via reference/materials.md). The D/G height ratio alone also falls in the crossover region near L_D of about 3 nm, where one ratio maps to two defect densities.

properties.name: L_D_nm
properties.source: graphene_defect_distance_from_ID_IG (Cancado et al. 2011) not applied: the laser wavelength is not stated (required input), and the G width of 24.8 cm-1 is outside the low-defect branch (validity L_D >= 10 nm, G about 14 cm-1).

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: graphene_strain_doping_from_G_2D (Lee et al. 2012) requires 513 to 516 nm excitation; laser wavelength unknown, so not applied. G at 1580.3 cm-1 is 1.3 cm-1 below the origin, within calibration uncertainty.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: Same as strain_sign: graphene_strain_doping_from_G_2D not applied without a 514.5 nm laser. G and 2D shifts are too small and uncalibrated to read doping.

citations: Ferrari, A. C. et al. Raman spectrum of graphene and graphene layers. Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 187401 (2006), arXiv cond-mat/0606284
Lee, J.-U., Yoon, D., Kim, H., Lee, S. W., Cheong, H. Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012) (strain-doping origin 1581.6 / 2676.9 cm-1), arXiv 1209.0234
Cancado, L. G. et al. Quantifying defects in graphene via Raman spectroscopy at different excitation energies. Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), arXiv 1105.0175
Bagheri, A. and Komsa, H.-P. Computational Raman Database. Sci. Data 10, 80 (2023), CC BY 4.0 (rows 2171, 2811 rejected)
limits: Laser wavelength not given (laser_nm null) and it was not inferred from the data. The 2D position (2681.2 cm-1) cannot be checked against the 514.5 nm reference, and the 2D band disperses by roughly 100 cm-1/eV. The strain/doping and L_D relations were therefore not applied.
Temperature 295 K: no correction applied. Heating from the laser is not estimated because the power is unknown.
Calibration: no Si line in the file, and the sampling is coarse (2.3 cm-1 per point). Peak positions are good to about 1 cm-1 at best and absolute shifts of 1 to 2 cm-1 cannot be trusted.

Layer number: the single-Lorentzian 2D rule gives monolayer, but the FWHM (35 to 40 cm-1) and I_2D/I_G (2.85 by height, 4.0 by area) do not match the monolayer reference cleanly on this Au substrate. Few-layer or turbostratic CVD graphene cannot be excluded from this spectrum alone. Substrate interference and metal contact (Au) can change I_2D/I_G, so it is not used alone.

Defect density: the D/G height ratio is 0.95 with a broad G band, so the sample is at the high-defect side of the Cancado curve. It is not possible to say from one ratio whether L_D is above or below about 3 nm without the laser wavelength and a width-based check.
D' (about 1620 cm-1) was not resolved as a separate band. It may be hidden on the G shoulder; the local refit did not detect it.
Broad background feature at about 3190 cm-1 (FWHM about 8400 cm-1) is a baseline or fluorescence component, not a Raman band, and was not reported as a peak.
Below about 50 cm-1 the data are the Rayleigh line and filter edge, which were excluded. Shear and breathing modes (layer-number check) cannot be assessed.
Au substrate: no Au Raman bands are expected in this range, and the substrate's effect on graphene (doping, strain, quenching) is not characterised by any reference in the library.
Backscattering geometry is assumed; no polarization series, so no polarization class is given.
Literature search with the Valency or iopic-bond tools was not run. The graphene reference values come from the curated tables (Lee 2012, Ferrari 2006, Cancado 2011) in the skill notes.
